name: Cursor
description: AI code editor where you review each agent change before accepting it. Disclosure: Cursor is bundled with The X Subscription (per Cursor's docs).
pricing: Free; Plus $8/mo (Cursor models only); Premium $30; Super $100; Ultra $200. Third-party models billed at API price.
verdict_reason: Cursor is for developers who want agents doing real work, in the editor and in the cloud. For most people, Premium at $30 a month is the plan worth paying for, because it's the first one with Cloud Agents, Automations, Origin, Bugbot and third-party models. Just know your bill can drift past the sticker price: included usage is a shared weekly pool, and third-party models draw on prepaid credit at API list price.
mobile_note: iOS app remote-controls agents; editor is desktop
mobile_description: The iOS app remote-controls agents. The editor is desktop-only.

overview.what_it_is: Cursor is an AI coding product built around agents. It includes Agent (in the editor and the command line), Chat, Cloud Agents, Automations, Bugbot code review and Origin code hosting. It's sold as part of "The X Subscription," one subscription that covers Grok, Cursor and X ([models and pricing](https://cursor.com/docs/models-and-pricing.md)).

whats_new.text: On Oct 13, 2026, Cursor launched the Origin App Marketplace, with 20+ apps for deployments, CI, code review, security, monitoring and project management. Anyone can submit an app: you create it in your namespace, build against the Origin API, then submit it for Cursor's review ([changelog](https://cursor.com/changelog)).

key_features: **Cloud agent canvases:** cloud agents can build interactive canvases, and you share a finished one by sending its link.
**Environments API (beta):** create and manage cloud agent environments programmatically. Environments support up to 300 repositories, and according to Cursor, large ones "load 5x faster."
**Remote control (Oct 6):** see and reply to local agents from the Cursor iOS app. Your computer has to stay on and online.
**Projects (Sep 10, beta):** a coordinator agent plans work and hands it off to subagents on a cloud computer.
**Rollouts and Security Review (Sep 23):** two bots, available on Teams and Enterprise only.
overview.getting_started: You can browse apps in the Origin App Marketplace now. To use remote control, download the Cursor iOS app, sign in and approve pairing in the desktop app. App builders should begin with the Origin publishing guide and API reference ([changelog](https://cursor.com/changelog)).

plans.name: Free
plans.detail: Agent and Chat with limited usage (the exact limit isn't stated)

plans.name: Premium
plans.detail: adds Cloud Agents, Automations, Origin, Bugbot and third-party models

good_to_know: Included usage is a weekly pool shared across Agent, Cloud Agents, Grok Bot and the Grok apps.
Third-party models are billed at API list price from prepaid credit. Teams and Enterprise also pay a Cursor Token Rate of $0.25 per 1M tokens.
Legacy plans (Hobby, Pro and others) continue for existing customers.
overview.disclosure: Drafted with AI assistance. No sponsorship.

name: Claude Code
description: Anthropic's terminal coding agent for multi-file refactors and features.
pricing: Included in paid Claude plans. Pro $20/mo ($17/mo billed annually); Max from $100/mo.
verdict_reason: Claude Code is for developers who want one agent that follows them across the terminal, VS Code, JetBrains, a desktop app and the browser, with the same CLAUDE.md files, settings and MCP servers on every surface. What stands out is how far it reaches past the editor: cloud scheduled tasks keep running when your computer is off, Remote Control lets you pick up a session from your phone, and an @Claude mention in Slack can turn a bug report into a pull request. Teams that script their workflows also get hooks, shareable skills and an Agent SDK for building their own agents on the same tools.
mobile_note: Claude mobile apps steer cloud/remote sessions; code doesn't run on-phone
mobile_description: Claude's mobile apps steer cloud and remote sessions. Code does not run on the phone.

name: OpenAI Codex
description: OpenAI's coding agent for local and background 'go fix this issue' tasks.
verdict_reason: Codex is for developers who want OpenAI's coding agent in the CLI, an IDE, a desktop app and the web, and who like a tool that ships often. October brought a lot: GPT-6.1 Sol became the default model in the CLI catalog, GPT-5.5 retired from ChatGPT-signed-in Codex on Oct 14, and CLI 0.163.0 (Oct 15) added a searchable /config panel, mid-response steering and parallel read-only tools. The desktop app also gained composer predictions in beta, which suggest your next prompt as an editable draft but never send it for you.
verdict_short: Runs in CLI, IDE, and web
mobile_note: ChatGPT mobile app steers Codex on your machines; preview
mobile_description: The ChatGPT mobile app steers Codex on your machines, and that control is in preview. The coding runs on your machines, not on the phone.

name: GitHub Copilot Pro
description: GitHub's AI pair programmer with agent mode inside popular editors.
pricing: Free, Pro $10, Pro+ $39, Max $100 a month.
verdict_reason: Copilot is for developers who already live on GitHub and want an assistant inside their editor, the CLI and pull requests rather than a separate tool. The pace on GitHub's changelog is the story this month: local sandboxing became generally available and Copilot CLI can now discover local models (Oct 7), Copilot can drive desktop apps with computer use (Oct 1), and new models such as Gemini 4 Argon and Claude Haiku 5.5 joined the picker. Agentic autofix for code scanning alerts also reached general availability on Oct 15, which matters most to teams that already run GitHub's security tooling.
mobile_note: Chat and cloud agent in GitHub Mobile; completions IDE-only
mobile_description: GitHub Mobile includes chat and the cloud agent. Completions are IDE-only.

name: Devin Desktop (formerly Windsurf)
description: Windsurf's editor, now Devin Desktop, plus Devin Cloud agents and the SWE-2 model.
pricing: Free (light quota); Pro $20/mo; Max $200/mo; Teams $80/mo + $40 per seat.
verdict_reason: Devin is for engineering teams that want an autonomous agent working in the cloud or on their own machine, testing in its own browser and carrying work through to a merge-ready PR. The release notes show where it's heading: Devin Oncall became generally available on Oct 19, watching Slack, Teams and PagerDuty to triage alerts and post a likely root cause, and Devin Review added Bitbucket Cloud support on Oct 21. It suits teams that want an agent on incidents and code review, not just new features.
mobile_note: Devin Mobile iOS app via waitlist only
mobile_description: A Devin Mobile iOS app is listed as waitlist-only. The official site doesn't confirm general mobile use, so check before relying on it.

name: Amazon Q Developer
description: AWS's AI coding assistant.
pricing: New signups stopped May 15, 2026. Support ends Apr 30, 2027.
verdict_reason: Amazon Q Developer is winding down. AWS stopped new signups on May 15, 2026, and the IDE plugins and paid subscriptions reach end of support on Apr 30, 2027. Existing Pro customers can still add users until then. AWS is steering developers to Kiro, its spec-driven IDE and CLI, which carries over agentic coding, inline chat and MCP support. Q Developer in the AWS Console, the docs and the Slack and Teams apps isn't affected. If you rely on its Java upgrades or .NET porting, AWS recommends finishing them before the cutoff.
mobile_note: Q chat in AWS Console Mobile App; coding in IDE
mobile_description: Q chat is in the AWS Console Mobile App. Coding stays in the IDE.

name: Tabnine
description: AI code assistant focused on enterprise deployment.
pricing: Pricing unverified.
verdict_reason: Tabnine is now part of Tricentis, and tabnine.com redirects to the Tricentis site, which points existing users to Tabnine's login, documentation and support. Tricentis presents itself as an agentic quality engineering platform for large enterprises, covering test creation, automation and performance testing under one control plane. That makes Tabnine a fit mainly for enterprise teams already in, or heading toward, the Tricentis ecosystem, not for individual developers shopping for a code assistant.
mobile_note: IDE plugin only (VS Code, JetBrains, Eclipse, Visual Studio)
mobile_description: Tabnine is an IDE plugin for VS Code, JetBrains, Eclipse, and Visual Studio. It is not offered on mobile.

name: Lovable
description: Chat-to-app builder for websites and web apps, no coding needed.
pricing: Free: 5 daily build credits (up to 30/mo). Pro $25/mo (100 credits); Business $50/mo. See lovable.dev/pricing.
verdict_reason: Lovable is for non-technical founders, small teams and classrooms who want to chat their way to a working web app, and now to its first users, without stitching tools together. Pay once the free 5 daily credits run dry on real projects, and note that the new Growth tools, which plan your launch and set up campaigns, add no fee beyond normal chat credits and your own ad spend. The catch is budgeting: costs vary by task, and credits expire on a schedule with no refunds, so monthly spend is harder to predict than with a flat-rate tool.
mobile_note: Official iOS and Android apps to create and continue projects
mobile_description: Official iOS and Android apps let you create and continue projects.

overview.what_it_is: Lovable describes itself as "an AI software engineer, which enables anyone to build for the web." In practice, you chat to build websites and web apps, with no technical knowledge needed. Workspaces allow unlimited members, so it suits individuals, teams, classrooms and communities. ([Lovable pricing](https://lovable.dev/pricing))

paragraphs: On October 14, Lovable added [Growth tools](https://docs.lovable.dev/changelog). You set a goal, such as "my first 100 signups," and Lovable builds a plan from your app, audience and traffic. It tells you what to fix first, and it says so when ads would be premature. It can set up tracking and campaigns on Google, YouTube, Facebook and Instagram, while you set the budget and approve spending. It also makes launch videos, demos, images and ad copy. Results appear in a redesigned Analytics view. Growth tools carry no extra fee. Standard chat costs apply, and Google or Meta bill your ad account directly.

Other changes from the past week include Sign in with Lovable for any website, self-restore of deleted projects within 60 days, workspace policies and an Action center, and the ability to create a Supabase project from Lovable. ([Lovable changelog](https://docs.lovable.dev/changelog))

key_features: Chat-based building for websites and web apps
Plan Mode for planning work at 1 credit per message
Web, desktop and iOS/Android apps, plus Slack and Telegram integrations
An MCP server you can use from Claude, Grok and other clients
You own your code and outputs, subject to third-party model rights
overview.getting_started: Lovable says "starting to build on Lovable is free." In Default Mode, cost varies with the task. Lovable's own examples are 0.50 credits to change a button style and 1.70 credits for a landing page with images. ([Lovable pricing](https://lovable.dev/pricing))
overview.pricing: Plans run from Free and Pro to Business and Enterprise, priced by included credits rather than per seat. The Free plan gives 5 build credits a day (up to 30 a month), plus 20 Cloud credits and 4 credits for AI features in your apps each month. Paid plans add monthly plan credits on top of the same daily and Cloud grants, and come in monthly and annual billing. See current prices on the [Lovable pricing page](https://lovable.dev/pricing). A [student discount](https://lovable.dev/students) is available.
good_to_know: Monthly credits expire 2 months after issue, annual credits 1 month after the annual period ends, and top-up credits after 12 months. Credits are non-refundable.
Hosting is usually covered by the included grant, but high-traffic apps draw on your credit balance.
API keys and the Action center need a Business or Enterprise plan. Workspace policies are Enterprise only.
overview.disclosure: Drafted with AI assistance. No sponsorship.

name: Bolt.new
description: Prompt-to-app builder in the browser by StackBlitz.
pricing: Pro $18/mo and Teams $27 per member/mo, both billed annually.
verdict_reason: Bolt.new is for product managers, founders, marketers and agencies who want to chat their way to a working website, app or prototype in the browser. You can start from a prompt, a Figma file, a GitHub repo or a team template. What stands out is how much comes built in: Bolt picks the model for each task, and Bolt Cloud adds hosting with analytics and custom domains, databases, user authentication and SEO tools, so a project can go live without separate accounts.
mobile_note: Mobile browser works; code view, visual edits, database desktop-only
mobile_description: The mobile browser works. Code view, visual edits, and the database are desktop-only.

name: v0
description: Vercel's AI app and UI builder.
pricing: Free (7 messages/day); Plus $30/user/mo; Business $100/user/mo; Premium $20 being sunset.
verdict_reason: v0 is Vercel's chat-based builder for apps and UI, aimed at people who want to go from prompt to a working React and Next.js project and collaborate on it. It has been shipping steadily: on Oct 6, personal accounts became team workspaces so anyone can invite collaborators, and on Oct 19 a Slack MCP integration arrived on all plans, letting v0 use a Slack thread as context or post updates. Since Sep 29, ChatGPT Plus and Pro subscribers can also connect their ChatGPT subscription to build in v0.
mobile_note: Official v0 iOS app
mobile_description: There is an official v0 app for iOS.

name: Replit
description: Cloud IDE with Replit Agent that builds and deploys apps from prompts.
pricing: Core $20/mo ($18 yearly); Pro $100/mo ($90 yearly). See replit.com/pricing.
verdict_reason: Replit is for builders who want to describe an app in plain language, let Agent build it and publish from the same project. Recent updates lean toward teams and enterprises. The Oct 16 changelog added Claude Haiku 5.5 to the model selector in Power Mode and a directory of Replit Solutions Partners, plus Bring Your Own Cloud: the full platform in your own cloud tenant (private preview), hosting published apps there, or exporting apps to self-host (both early access).
verdict_short: Builds the app, then you publish
mobile_note: iOS and Android apps with Agent
mobile_description: The iOS and Android apps include Agent.

name: Base44
description: AI app builder for building apps from natural language.
pricing: Free (25 message credits/mo). Starter $16/mo, Builder $40/mo, Pro $80/mo, Elite $160/mo.
verdict_reason: Base44 is for non-coders who want to build apps, websites and AI agents in their own words without setting up servers, databases or payments, because backend, storage, auth, hosting and payments are already built in. What stands out is that it doesn't stop at launch: there are built-in marketing tools such as an SEO/GEO dashboard, plus design controls that set colors and fonts across the whole app at once. You can also create agents that connect to your tools and run around the clock.
mobile_note: iOS app plus full building in mobile browser
mobile_description: An iOS app is available, and the mobile browser supports full building.

name: n8n
description: Fair-code workflow automation with an AI Agent node; self-hostable.
pricing: Self-host free; Cloud Starter €20/mo billed annually (2,500 executions); Pro €50/mo.
verdict_reason: n8n is for technical teams who want AI agents and workflows they can follow step by step. You can open any step, see what it did and explain it to whoever runs it. It's strongest for repeat operations work such as refunds, onboarding or threat triage, where an agent step sits inside a larger, auditable workflow with human approvals in Slack.
mobile_note: Web editor has touch support; no official mobile app
mobile_description: The web editor has touch support. There is no official mobile app.

name: AI by Zapier
description: Zapier's AI step, formerly Zapier Agents, that reasons and acts with tools inside any Zap.
pricing: Agents Pro $33.33/mo billed annually ($400/yr), 1,500 activities (zapier.com/pricing).
verdict_reason: Zapier Agents became AI by Zapier on Oct 6, 2026. The agent's tool calling, reasoning and autonomous actions now run as a single AI step inside the Zap editor, so they can use any of Zapier's 9,000+ app triggers, filters, paths and Zap History. It's for teams already automating in Zapier who want an agent inside their existing workflows. New since the move: you can require approval per tool, not just all-or-nothing, and pick a model tier or a specific model for each step. Eligible agents are converted to Zaps automatically.
mobile_note: Web app; no official mobile statement found
mobile_description: This is a web app, and the official site doesn't say whether it works on mobile, so check before relying on it.

name: Make
description: Visual automation platform with credit-based scenarios.
pricing: Pricing unverified.
verdict_reason: Make is for teams that want to build automations and AI agents on one visual canvas and see everything running in one place. You can build by prompting, by drag-and-drop, or from Claude, ChatGPT and Gemini through its MCP server, and drop into JavaScript or Python when needed. It connects to 3,500+ apps, and AI agents show their reasoning against the goals, tools and limits you set. For larger organizations, role-based access, audit logs and SOC 2 Type II and SOC 3 certification are the draw.
mobile_note: iOS/Android companion apps for device triggers only
mobile_description: The iOS and Android companion apps are for device triggers only.

name: Activepieces
description: Open-source automation platform with AI pieces.
pricing: Free 1,000 credits/mo, Plus $20/mo.
verdict_reason: Activepieces is for teams that want chat, AI agents, flows and tables in one open-source workspace, connected to 760+ apps. It runs in the cloud or self-hosted. It also offers an MCP server, so your pieces are usable from the AI tools people already work in, and it pitches enterprise control for teams rolling AI out beyond a single power user.
mobile_note: No official mobile info found
mobile_description: The official site doesn't say whether it works on mobile, so check before relying on it.

name: Gumloop
description: AI workflow builder billing at cost of tokens and tools plus a fee.
pricing: No free plan (14-day trial); Pro $37/mo (20,000 credits) plus 8% orchestration fee.
verdict_reason: Gumloop is for go-to-market, support and operations teams that want to build, share and control AI agents connected to tools like Slack, HubSpot, Gong, Gmail and Salesforce. Each agent gets its own model, instructions, connectors and reusable skills. What stands out is the oversight layer Gumloop shows off, with views of AI spend, usage by model provider and adoption by teammate, which suits companies rolling agents out across many people.
mobile_note: No official mobile app info; texting Gumball documented
mobile_description: The official docs don't describe a mobile app, though texting Gumball is documented. The official site doesn't say whether the product works on a phone, so check before relying on it.

name: Lindy
description: Prebuilt AI assistant you customize; positioned as a Slack-native teammate.
pricing: Team billed monthly per active user (see lindy.ai/pricing for the current rate); 7-day trial with $50 credits.
verdict_reason: Lindy is for small teams who live in Slack, email and calendars and want one assistant to handle inboxes, scheduling and calls. It's worth a seat once you have repeat tasks it can learn and run on a schedule, or a phone line for it to answer, not just the odd one-off request. Watch the credits: monthly ones don't roll over, so plan for what your team will use each month.
mobile_note: Vendor site lists iOS/Android; no current store listing found
mobile_description: The vendor site lists iOS and Android, but no current store listing was found. The official site doesn't confirm mobile support, so check before relying on it.

overview.what_it_is: [Lindy](https://www.lindy.ai/) is an AI assistant built to work like a teammate. It works inside Slack, Gmail (through a Chrome extension), email, chat, text and phone, and handles inbox management, meetings, scheduling, briefs and routines. It connects to more than 1,500 integrations and supports MCP.

items: **Watch and Learn (Oct 12):** record your screen for up to an hour, or write out the steps. Lindy learns the task and then runs it on request or on a schedule.

**Phone calls (Oct 14):** Lindy gets its own phone number. It can place calls for you, such as rescheduling an appointment or booking a table, and report back. It can also answer as a receptionist, take messages and book callers onto your calendar. Numbers are US and Canada only.

**Booking links (Oct 16):** scheduling links that Lindy positions as a Calendly replacement. You can set each link's length, hours, breaks and video app, and add a logo or make it single-use. Guests don't need a Lindy account, and meetings land on Google or Outlook calendars.
**New integrations (Oct 18):** Airtable, Intercom, Google Analytics, ClickUp, Luma and expanded Slack support, plus quick-question forms.

key_features: **Works where you do:** Slack, Gmail, email, chat, text and phone, with 1,500+ integrations.
**Approval for outside actions:** anything with outside impact waits for your OK.
Per Lindy, your data isn't used for training, and the company says it is SOC 2 and GDPR compliant.
overview.getting_started: Sign up for a 7-day trial: $50 in credits that last 7 days, no credit card needed. Teammates who join through Slack get a 7-day trial before their seat is billed. Direct signups are billed right away.

items: **Free trial:** a 7-day trial with $50 in credits that last 7 days. There is no ongoing free plan.

**Team:** billed monthly per active user, with credits pooled across the team. See the [pricing page](https://www.lindy.ai/pricing) for the current rate. Top-ups are $10 per 1,000 credits. The plan includes per-task model choice, computer use and live onboarding.
**Enterprise:** custom pricing. Adds HIPAA/BAA, SSO and SCIM, audit logs and dedicated support.

good_to_know: Monthly credits refresh each cycle and don't roll over. Top-up credits don't expire, and there's no mid-cycle proration.
When credits run out, Lindy pauses credit-using actions rather than charging overage.
overview.disclosure: Drafted with AI assistance. No sponsorship.

name: Manus
description: Autonomous general agent for one-off research and analysis tasks.
pricing: Pricing unverified.
verdict_reason: Manus is a general-purpose agent for people who want to hand off whole tasks such as research, slides, websites, video and design. Manus 2.0 launched on Sep 28, 2026 with a new agent harness called Cascade, a Cloud Computer and Automations, Manus Studio for professional creation and Cue, a separate app for personal agents. Since then it has added Manus Flex for using your own API key (Sep 29) and a Video Editor and Game Dev mode (Oct 1).
mobile_note: iOS and Android apps
mobile_description: Manus has official iOS and Android apps.

name: Microsoft Copilot Studio
description: Low-code agent builder for Microsoft 365.
pricing: $200/mo per 25,000 Copilot Credits, or pay as you go.
verdict_reason: Copilot Studio is for organizations on Microsoft 365 that want to build their own agents and workflows grounded in company data. September's releases focus on workflows. An extract node pulls values and tables out of invoices and contracts, and a Copilot node (preview) runs Copilot Chat or Cowork tasks grounded in a user's mail, files and calendar. Agents can also now read Excel, PowerPoint and Word attachments and use Dataverse tables as knowledge, and makers can pick models from a dropdown and run content safety tests.
mobile_note: Web maker; no official mobile support statement found
mobile_description: This is a web maker, and the official site doesn't say whether it works on mobile, so check before relying on it.

name: OpenAI Agent Builder
description: Visual canvas for multi-step agent workflows.
pricing: Shutting down Nov 30, 2026; use the Agents SDK or ChatGPT Workspace Agents.
verdict_reason: Agent Builder is shutting down. OpenAI announced the deprecation on Jun 3, 2026, and the visual canvas is scheduled to shut down on Nov 30, 2026. OpenAI's migration guide points existing users to the Agents SDK, for building in code, or to ChatGPT Workspace Agents. ChatKit stays available. This page is useful only if you still have flows to move.
mobile_note: Web platform tool; no mobile statement found
mobile_description: This is a web tool, and the official site doesn't say whether it works on mobile, so check before relying on it.

name: Dify
description: Platform for building LLM apps and agents, with a cloud Sandbox tier.
pricing: Sandbox is free. Professional is $590 per workspace a year.
verdict_reason: Dify is for teams building LLM apps, agentic workflows and RAG chatbots who want a visual builder plus the option to self-host. There's an open-source Community Edition for Docker, a hosted cloud and a private Enterprise deployment. Its newest piece, announced Aug 27, 2026, is a New Agent you build by chatting. Dify turns the conversation into reusable skills and keeps the context, and you can run the finished agent as its own app or drop it into a larger workflow.
mobile_note: Published web apps responsive; builder mobile support unstated
mobile_description: Published web apps are described as responsive. The official site doesn't say whether the builder works on mobile, so check before relying on it.

name: Godot AI
description: Free MIT plugin connecting Claude Code, Codex and other agents to a running Godot editor (46 tools).
pricing: Free, open source (MIT). Needs Godot 4.7+; telemetry on by default.
verdict_reason: Godot AI is for Godot developers who want Claude Code, Codex or another MCP client to work directly in a running Godot editor. It's free and open source under the MIT license. Its 46 tools and 120+ operations let an agent build scenes, edit nodes and scripts, wire signals, and set up UI, materials, animation, particles, cameras and environments. GDScript is fully supported, while C# is text-only. It needs Godot 4.7 or later, and usage telemetry is on unless you turn it off with an environment variable. The latest release is v4.3.0 (Oct 3).
mobile_note: MCP server and Godot editor tools only
mobile_description: Godot AI is an MCP server and a set of Godot editor tools. It does not run as a mobile app.

name: Unity AI agent plugin
description: Unity's official agent plugin for Claude Code, Codex and Grok Build (Unity 6+).
pricing: Unity AI bundled with Unity Personal (free) or Pro ($210/mo/seat).
verdict_reason: Unity's official plugin is for Unity 6+ developers who already work through a coding agent. It now ships for Claude Code, Codex and Grok Build, which Unity added as the third agent. All three get the same 30+ skills written by Unity's own feature teams, covering UI Toolkit and uGUI, 2D, URP and Shader Graph, physics, IAP, multiplayer, web and localization. Because Unity maintains them from one repository, a team mixing agents gets the same Unity guidance from each. Setup is one terminal command.
mobile_note: CLI coding-agent plugin for Unity editor
mobile_description: This is a command-line coding-agent plugin for the Unity editor. It does not run as a mobile app.

name: Scenario
description: Game art generator that trains models on your own style.
pricing: 50 free daily credits (non-commercial); Starter $15/mo, Pro $45, Max $75. See scenario.com/pricing.
verdict_reason: Scenario is for game and creative teams that need on-style assets at volume. It puts image, video, 3D and audio models in one browser workspace, and you can train custom models on your own art so characters and style hold from shot to shot. What stands out is the range of ways in: the app, node-based workflows, agents, and an MCP server and API for your own pipeline. That lets a studio move from one-off generation to repeatable asset production, including turning an image into a textured, rigged 3D model for your engine.
verdict_short: Train a model on your art
mobile_note: Browser platform; only third-party mention of mobile app
mobile_description: A mobile app is mentioned only by a third party. The official site doesn't say whether it works on mobile, so check before relying on it.

name: Meshy
description: Text- and image-to-3D model generation.
pricing: Free 100 credits/mo, Pro $20, Premium $40, Studio $70 per seat, Ultra $100.
verdict_reason: Meshy is for game developers, 3D printers and product designers who want 3D models from a text prompt, image or sketch. Meshy 7.1 is now live and focuses on true-to-reference results. Beyond generation, it handles PBR texturing, auto-rigging and animation, and plugs into Blender, Unity, Bambu Studio and Creality Print. Developers can reach it through an API, a CLI, or an MCP server that generates 3D inside Claude, Cursor and other agents.
mobile_note: Official iOS and Android apps
mobile_description: Meshy has official iOS and Android apps.

name: Layer AI
description: Usage-based art production platform for game studios, unlimited seats.
pricing: From $10/mo for 300 Creative Units.
verdict_reason: Layer is for game and creative studios that want one place to make and edit art with many models: 130+ image models plus video tools. What stands out is the editing toolkit around generation. You can change a scene's camera angle or lighting, swap objects, split images into movable layers, vectorize to SVG, and keep a whole cast in one art direction. It suits studios that want generation and cleanup in the same tool.
mobile_note: No official mobile info found
mobile_description: The official site doesn't say whether it works on mobile, so check before relying on it.

name: Rosebud AI
description: No-code builder for playable browser games from prompts.
pricing: Free plan with 8,000 credits (weekly refill in eligible regions); paid tiers available.
verdict_reason: Rosebud is for beginners, educators and game-jam makers who want to describe a game and get something playable in the browser, or start from a template. It covers 3D games, RPGs, visual novels and interactive stories, with AI NPCs and asset generators for sprites, sprite sheets, 3D models and skyboxes. Rosebud also offers free game hosting, which makes it a gentle first step into building and sharing games with AI.
verdict_short: Free way to try a game
mobile_note: Vendor says browser maker works on phones and tablets
mobile_description: The vendor says the browser maker works on phones and tablets.

name: Inworld
description: Real-time voice and speech API for AI characters and NPCs.
pricing: Free on-demand tier (70 min TTS); Creator $25/mo.
verdict_reason: Inworld is for developers building voice-driven apps or games who want speech and open-model LLM inference on one bill, behind an API that already works with the OpenAI SDK. The free On-Demand tier and browser playground cover early experiments, and a paid plan makes sense once you need more concurrent requests or lower TTS rates, which drop at each tier from Creator at $25 a month up to Growth. Don't size up too early, though: credits roll over for only three months on a paid plan and are forfeited if you downgrade.
mobile_note: Browser Studio; only on-device TTS SDK for mobile
mobile_description: The official site documents an on-device text-to-speech SDK for mobile. It doesn't say whether Browser Studio works on a phone, so check before relying on it.

overview.what_it_is: [Inworld](https://inworld.ai/pricing) is a voice and LLM platform for developers. It offers text-to-speech (TTS-2 and TTS-2 Flash), speech-to-text, speech-to-speech and LLM inference, all paid from one credit balance. Its new Inworld Inference is, in Inworld's words, "an LLM inference API for consumer apps," serving open models such as Gemma 4, GLM, DeepSeek and MiMo.

whats_new.text: On Oct 14, 2026, Inworld opened [Inworld Inference](https://inworld.ai/blog/introducing-inworld-inference) to every developer, including a new Fast tier with realtime decoding.

key_features: An OpenAI-compatible API with streaming support.

Four service tiers you choose per request, API key or workspace: Flex (lowest price, fails fast and unbilled when busy), Default (no rate limits), Priority (uptime commitment) and Fast (realtime decoding).
A router for fallback models, conditional rules and weighted A/B splits.
Dedicated deployments where you can bring your own weights.
Zero data retention on hosted models, with LLM inference running in the US.
overview.getting_started: Point the OpenAI SDK at `https://api.inworld.ai/v1`, add your Inworld API key and pick a model ID such as `inworld/models/gemma-4-26b-a4b-it`. You can also try any model in the browser playground without an API key.

pricing.text: [Inworld's pricing](https://inworld.ai/pricing) starts with On-Demand at $0, pay as you go, which includes up to 70 minutes of TTS or 400 minutes of STT free. Paid plans are Creator at $25 a month, Builder at $100, Developer at $300 and Growth at $1,500, each granting the same amount in monthly credits. Enterprise is custom.

plans.name: On-Demand
plans.detail: pay as you go, which includes up to 70 minutes of TTS or 400 minutes of STT free

pricing.note: TTS-2 runs from $25 per 1M characters on On-Demand down to $12.50 on Growth. LLM inference starts at $0.07 per 1M input tokens; Gemma 4 26B costs $0.07 input and $0.34 output per 1M tokens at Default rates. Yearly billing gives two months free.

good_to_know: Monthly credits roll over for up to three months while you're on a paid plan, and downgrading forfeits remaining credits.
Concurrent requests range from 5 on On-Demand to 500 on Growth.
Every plan includes a commercial license, plus GDPR and SOC 2 Type II compliance. EU and India data residency are Enterprise only.
overview.disclosure: Drafted with AI assistance. No sponsorship.

name: Leonardo AI
description: 2D image generator for concept art, textures and key art.
pricing: Free 150 fast tokens a day; Essential $12/mo.
verdict_reason: Leonardo is for artists, designers and marketing teams who want images and video from prompts or custom models, then refine them without starting over. It brings in-house models such as Lucid Origin and Lucid Realism together with third-party models such as Nano Banana Pro, Seedream 4.5, FLUX.2 Pro and Ideogram 3.0. Editing tools are built to keep characters, composition and style intact, and upscaling prepares assets for print. For game work, that means concept and key art, with a developer API when you need it in a pipeline.
mobile_note: iOS and Android apps
mobile_description: Leonardo AI has iOS and Android apps.

name: Ludo.ai
description: Game concepting and market research assistant.
pricing: Indie $15/mo, Pro $35/mo, Studio $300/mo, all billed annually.
verdict_reason: Ludo.ai is for indie developers and small studios who want game-ready assets from one place: sprites and animations, icons, UI, textures, music, 3D and video. What stands out is that it's built as an asset pipeline rather than a one-off generator, with MCP access for working from your own tools and a showcase of shipped games made with its output.
mobile_note: Mobile-web claim only in press release, not vendor docs
mobile_description: A mobile-web claim appears in a press release, not in the vendor docs. The official site doesn't confirm mobile support, so check before relying on it.

name: ElevenLabs
description: AI voice generation for voiceover, dialogue and sound.
pricing: Free; Starter $6/mo with a commercial license.
verdict_reason: ElevenLabs is for game developers, creators and companies that need expressive AI voices for narration, character dialogue, dubbing and voice agents. The big recent change is Eleven v4, which ElevenLabs calls its most emotive model yet, released with Eleven v4 Turbo on Sep 28. The platform also covers music, speech to text, voice cloning and the ElevenAgents platform for conversational agents. ElevenAgents keeps shipping: on Oct 12 it added merging and searching of triage tickets.
mobile_note: iOS and Android apps
mobile_description: ElevenLabs has iOS and Android apps.

name: Recursive Flint
description: An open-weight coding model from Recursive, with 39.8B total parameters and about 2.5B active per token, built for coding agents that investigate codebases, fix bugs and write tests. It's Apache-2.0 and ships with an SGLang serving kit.
pricing: Free open weights (Apache 2.0). The model card says hosted API terms are separate, and it states no API price.
verdict_reason: Recursive Flint is for self-hosters who want a fast coding model. Recursive reports 74.2% on SWE-bench Verified and 54.9% on Terminal-Bench 2.1, and those scores are self-reported. It's an 80 GB download that needs one B300 or H200 GPU per replica for now. On a Mac, the indie engine Kapitsa already runs it.
mobile_note: Runs on one B300 or H200 GPU per replica, not on phones
mobile_description: The model card says it runs on one B300 or H200 GPU per replica (an 80 GB download), and quantized variants are for NVIDIA and Apple Silicon computers, not phones.
pick_reason: Open-weight coding model with 39.8B parameters and about 2.5B active per token

name: Mercury 3
description: A diffusion-based LLM that Inception says runs at more than 1,000 tokens per second with a 1M-token context window. It's OpenAI API compatible and available on Inception's API, OpenRouter, Baseten and Vercel.
pricing: $0.20 per 1M input tokens and $0.70 per 1M output tokens. It's 50% off at launch ($0.10/$0.35), and cached tokens are 90% off the input price.
verdict_reason: Mercury 3 is for browser agents, voice bots and subagents where speed matters more than raw intelligence. Inception claims 1,068 tokens per second on NVIDIA GPUs, a 1M-token context window and quality on par with GPT-6 Luna and Claude Haiku 5.5. All benchmarks are Inception's own. It costs $0.20/$0.70 per million input/output tokens, and is half that during launch.
mobile_note: No official mobile info found
mobile_description: The official site doesn't say whether it works on mobile, so check before relying on it.
pick_reason: Diffusion LLM that Inception says runs at more than 1,000 tokens per second

name: Voxtral 3
description: Mistral's speech-to-text and text-to-speech models plus a voice agent SDK that listens, reasons, calls tools and speaks in one real-time pipeline. Transcription covers 50+ languages, and you can use Mistral's EU-hosted API or self-deploy.
pricing: The announcement gives one price: Voxtral Mini Transcribe 3 at $0.0035 per minute. No other prices are listed in the post.
verdict_reason: Voxtral 3 is for phone and support agents, especially in Europe or anywhere audio has to stay on your own infrastructure. Transcription covers 50+ languages, the new TTS voices cover 35+ languages, and Pro Voice adapts a voice from 30 minutes of audio. Comparisons with Whisper and others are Mistral's own.
mobile_note: Agents work over phone or web; no mobile app stated
mobile_description: Mistral says the agents work over phone or web, meaning phone calls, not a mobile app. The official site doesn't say whether it works on mobile, so check before relying on it.
pick_reason: Speech models and a voice agent SDK that listen, reason, call tools and speak

name: earshot
description: Gives coding agents "ears": it describes sounds in words, finds moments in long recordings and critiques the audio of whole videos. It runs locally on CPU as a CLI, Python API and MCP server.
use_cases: Describing a sound file in words
Finding a moment in a long recording
pricing: Free, open source (MIT).
verdict_reason: earshot is for anyone having an agent build demos, launch videos or game audio. It describes a sound file in words, finds a specific moment in a long recording and writes a second-by-second listening report on a whole video. The descriptions are useful evidence, not a replacement for listening yourself.
mobile_note: Local CLI, Python API, and MCP server; no mobile app stated
mobile_description: The official site doesn't say whether it works on mobile, so check before relying on it.
pick_reason: Gives coding agents ears for sound files, long recordings and whole videos

name: fx0
description: An open-source design agent: describe a page and it writes the whole thing as a single HTML file, keeping a version for every turn. It starts from ten design styles or your own design.md.
pricing: Free and open source (Apache-2.0). Model calls bill through your own Vercel AI Gateway when you sign in with Vercel. A deployment can optionally offer five free prompts per IP.
verdict_reason: fx0 is for landing pages and mockups, and a readable example if you want to build your own agent app on Vercel's libfx. You describe a page and it writes the whole thing as one HTML file, keeping a version for every turn. Model costs bill through your Vercel AI Gateway account, and each turn is capped at 64 model steps so a looping agent can't run up a bill.
mobile_note: No official mobile info found
mobile_description: The official site doesn't say whether it works on mobile, so check before relying on it.
pick_reason: Describe a page and it writes the whole thing as one HTML file

name: Beam
description: Brings windows from another Mac, such as agents running on a headless Mac mini, onto the Mac in front of you as real windows with their own Dock icons. Traffic goes directly between your Macs, encrypted.
use_cases: Pulling remote Mac windows onto your Mac
pricing: Free ($0, 20 minutes a day). Yearly is $7/month, billed $84 a year. Lifetime is $199. Team pricing is shown per seat.
verdict_reason: Beam is for anyone running agents on a headless Mac who is tired of Screen Sharing. Windows arrive as real windows, each with a Dock icon, and traffic goes directly between your Macs, encrypted. It needs two Macs on macOS Sonoma or later, Apple silicon or Intel. The free tier gives you 20 minutes a day. The yearly plan is $84 ($7 a month), and lifetime is $199.
mobile_note: A share link opens one window in a phone browser; the app needs two Macs
mobile_description: Beam's FAQ says a share link opens one window in any browser, on any device, so you can view a window from a phone browser, but the app itself needs two Macs on macOS Sonoma or later, Apple silicon or Intel.
pick_reason: Pulls windows from another Mac onto yours as real windows with Dock icons

name: CleanYourTV
description: A prompt and a small launcher that let Claude Code, Codex or Gemini CLI debloat an Android or Google TV over Wi-Fi and swap in an ad-free, Apple TV-style home screen. Apps are disabled rather than uninstalled, and there's a one-line restore.
use_cases: Debloating an Android or Google TV
pricing: Free, open source (MIT license file). You need your own coding assistant.
verdict_reason: CleanYourTV is for reviving an old Android or Google TV without buying new hardware. You need access to Claude Code, Codex or Gemini CLI. The agent connects over ADB, disables apps rather than deleting them, and keeps a restore script. TV Detox's own prompt warns that a few TVs got stuck at the logo or kept restarting. Keep the restore script handy, and don't do this to a TV you can't afford to fiddle with.
mobile_note: Needs a computer on the same Wi-Fi as the TV
mobile_description: The README says you need a computer on the same Wi-Fi as the TV and a coding assistant with shell access.
pick_reason: Lets Claude Code, Codex or Gemini CLI debloat an Android or Google TV over Wi-Fi

name: TV Detox
description: A copy-paste prompt and a tiny home screen that let Claude Code or Codex clean up a slow Android TV, asking before every change and keeping an undo list. Its prompt warns that a few TVs have gotten stuck at the logo.
use_cases: Cleaning up a slow Android TV
pricing: Free, open source (MIT).
verdict_reason: TV Detox is a similar project to CleanYourTV that appeared within days. You paste its prompt into Claude Code or Codex, and it asks before every change, turns apps off instead of deleting them, and keeps an undo list. Its prompt warns that a few TVs got stuck at the logo or kept restarting.
mobile_note: You run it on a laptop on the same Wi-Fi as the TV
mobile_description: You run Claude Code or Codex on your laptop, which has to be on the same Wi-Fi as the TV.
pick_reason: A prompt and tiny home screen that let Claude Code or Codex clean up a slow Android TV

name: Co-op Anything
description: A playbook, skills and an MCP server that let a coding agent turn a single-player PC game into co-op, by reviving an existing mod or reverse engineering the game, then testing with in-game bots. It hosts no game files and avoids anti-cheat and online services.
pricing: Free, open source (MIT).
verdict_reason: Co-op Anything is for modders and anyone with a stack of single-player favorites. You tell Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or another agent which game you want to play with friends, and it follows the repo's playbook: look for an existing co-op mod and fix it, or reverse engineer the game and build one, then test with bots and package a one-click install so friends can join over Steam. Results will vary a lot by game. This is modding, not a button press.
mobile_note: Targets PC games, with friends joining over Steam
mobile_description: The README targets games that run on your PC, with friends joining over Steam.
pick_reason: Lets a coding agent turn a single-player PC game into co-op

name: Snyk
description: Security platform covering open-source dependencies (SCA), code (SAST), infrastructure as code and containers.
use_cases: Real-time code scanning in IDE, CLI and source control
pricing: Free $0/mo; Team starts at $25/mo (billed monthly; up to 10 developers); Enterprise is credit-based, contact sales. Evo agentic features need an Enterprise Platform Subscription.
verdict_reason: Snyk is a good fit if you want dependency, code, IaC and container checks in one place, and the Free plan lets you try it from your IDE or CLI. The Team plan starts at $25 a month, billed monthly, for up to 10 developers. The newer Evo AI agents sit behind an Enterprise subscription, so smaller teams won't see those.
mobile_note: The official site doesn't mention a mobile app or mobile use, so this isn't confirmed.
mobile_description: The official site doesn't mention a mobile app or mobile use.

name: Semgrep
description: Code scanning platform for SAST, supply chain (SCA) and secrets detection, with AI-assisted triage and fixes.
use_cases: Static code analysis with custom rules
pricing: Free for up to 10 contributors and 10 private repos; Teams: Code $30, Supply Chain $30, Secrets $15 per contributor/month; Enterprise custom.
verdict_reason: Semgrep lets you buy only what you need: code scanning, supply chain, or secrets, each priced per contributor. The free edition covers up to 10 contributors, which is plenty for a small team to get a real feel for it. If you run it locally or in your own CI, your source code stays on your machines.
mobile_note: The official site doesn't mention a mobile app or mobile use, so this isn't confirmed.
mobile_description: The official site doesn't mention a mobile app or mobile use.

name: Socket
description: Supply-chain security that detects and blocks malicious or risky open-source dependencies.
pricing: Free $0 (1 dev seat); Team $25/dev seat/mo (from 5 seats); Business $50/dev seat/mo (from 20 seats); Enterprise custom. Yearly billing saves up to 20%. Free for open source.
verdict_reason: Socket focuses on the packages you pull in, and can block malicious ones before they land. The free plan covers one developer with unlimited repositories, and Socket says it will always be free for open-source projects. Only your list of dependencies is sent to Socket, not your source code.
mobile_note: The official site doesn't mention a mobile app or mobile use, so this isn't confirmed.
mobile_description: The official site doesn't mention a mobile app or mobile use.

name: GitGuardian
description: Secrets detection and non-human identity (NHI) security across code, CI/CD and developer tools.
use_cases: Monitoring public GitHub leaks (limited on Growth, unlimited on Enterprise; not on Starter)
pricing: Starter: free $0 for up to 25 devs; Growth and Enterprise: contact sales (prices not public).
verdict_reason: GitGuardian does one job, finding secrets that leak, across repos, CI/CD and containers. The free Starter plan works for teams of up to 25 developers and includes real-time scanning. Developer-machine protection and public leak monitoring are paid features, and the Growth and Enterprise plans aren't priced publicly, so expect a sales conversation once you need them.
mobile_note: The official site doesn't mention a mobile app or mobile use, so this isn't confirmed.
mobile_description: The official site doesn't mention a mobile app or mobile use.

name: Lakera
description: AI security platform for runtime protection of GenAI apps and agents, workforce AI use and AI red teaming.
pricing: Lakera Guard Community $0/mo (10k requests/month, 8k-token prompts, SaaS); Enterprise: contact sales.
verdict_reason: Lakera sits between your users and your AI app, screening for prompt injection, jailbreaks and data leaks. The free Community plan gives you 10,000 requests a month, enough to wire it into a prototype and see how it behaves. Self-hosting, SSO and SIEM integration come with Enterprise.
mobile_note: The official site doesn't mention a mobile app or mobile use, so this isn't confirmed.
mobile_description: The official site doesn't mention a mobile app or mobile use.

name: NVIDIA NeMo Guardrails
description: Open-source toolkit for adding programmable guardrails to LLM-based conversational applications.
pricing: Free, open source (Apache 2.0).
verdict_reason: NeMo Guardrails is a free, open-source Python library for setting rules on what your LLM app will and won't do. You install it with pip and write the rails yourself, so it suits developers who want full control. It's Apache 2.0 licensed, so you can use it commercially.
mobile_note: The official site doesn't mention a mobile app or mobile use, so this isn't confirmed.
mobile_description: The official site doesn't mention a mobile app or mobile use.

name: GitHub Advanced Security
description: GitHub's paid security add-ons: Secret Protection and Code Security (code scanning, Copilot Autofix, dependency review).
pricing: Two separate add-ons, each per active committer/month and requiring GitHub Team or Enterprise: Secret Protection $19 (secret scanning, push protection, custom patterns) and Code Security $30 (CodeQL code scanning, Copilot Autofix, dependency review). Code and secret scanning are on by default for public repos.
verdict_reason: If your code already lives on GitHub, secret scanning and code scanning run where your pull requests already are. Public repositories get code and secret scanning by default. For private repos you'll need a Team or Enterprise plan plus one or both add-ons: Secret Protection ($19) and Code Security ($30), each priced per active committer per month.
mobile_note: The official site doesn't mention a mobile app or mobile use, so this isn't confirmed.
mobile_description: The official site doesn't mention a mobile app or mobile use.

name: VS Code
description: Code editor. The 1.143 release notes add a Compare models preview that sends one task to two or more models, with optional Judge and Synthesize steps.
use_cases: Sending one task to two or more models
Comparing agent attempts side by side
pricing: Free, built on open source.
verdict_reason: VS Code is for developers who want coding agents in the editor. The 1.143 notes add a Compare models preview in the Agents window. You select two or more models, send them one prompt, and each attempt runs in its own session. A Judge model is optional: it scores the attempts and recommends a solution. Synthesize, which builds on the recommended attempt with ideas from the others, starts only when you request it. The preview stays off until you enable sessions.chat.compareAgents.enabled.
mobile_note: VS Code for the Web runs on phones and tablets; small screens have limits
mobile_description: Official docs say VS Code for the Web can run on tablets such as iPads, and on mobile devices, though smaller screens may have limitations.

name: WorldTUI
description: A 360M-parameter model trained to act as a terminal, predicting the next screen from each keypress. A 208 MB demo runs in the browser.
use_cases: Predicting a terminal screen from keypresses
Trying the demo in a browser
pricing: Pricing unverified.
verdict_reason: WorldTUI is for anyone who wants to see a small model act as a terminal. The October 21, 2026 post says a 360M-parameter model, fine-tuned from Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B, takes each keypress and predicts the next screen, with no shell or filesystem behind it. The browser demo is the int4 build at 208 MB. The post says it should work on a modern phone, but painfully slowly, and that it is designed for a desktop browser with WebGPU and a physical keyboard.
mobile_note: Browser demo works on a modern phone, painfully slowly
mobile_description: The post says the demo should work on a modern phone, but painfully slowly. It is designed for a desktop browser with WebGPU and a physical keyboard.

name: qwen3-4b-deslop
description: A Qwen3-4B fine-tune that drops common AI writing tics. The author reports the slop score fell from 121 to 12.5 per 1,000 words. It runs locally with Ollama.
use_cases: Local drafts without common AI writing tics
Running a small model with Ollama
pricing: Pricing unverified.
verdict_reason: qwen3-4b-deslop is a fine-tune of Qwen3-4B-Instruct for people who want a small local model with fewer assistant writing habits. The author reports that on 40 prompts held out of training, the slop score fell from 121 to 12.5 per 1,000 words, and em dashes fell from 20.5 per 1,000 words to zero. The Q4_K_M weights are a 2.5 GB download and run locally with Ollama or llama.cpp. The post says the voice is flat and the model still invents names and places.
mobile_note: The official site doesn't mention a mobile app or mobile use, so this isn't confirmed.
mobile_description: The official site doesn't mention a mobile app or mobile use.

name: Kapitsa
description: Inference engine for Apple silicon that runs Qwen and Nemotron models locally, with OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible APIs. Apache-2.0.
use_cases: Local Qwen and Nemotron models for coding agents
pricing: Free, open source (Apache 2.0).
verdict_reason: Kapitsa is for people who want Qwen or Nemotron running locally on a Mac and wired to a coding agent. The README says it also runs Recursive's Flint, serves OpenAI and Anthropic APIs, and can start OpenCode, Claude Code, Codex, or pi on a local model. It requires a Mac with Apple silicon (M1 or newer) and macOS 14 Sonoma or later. The license is Apache-2.0.
mobile_note: Requires a Mac with Apple silicon and macOS 14 or later
mobile_description: The README requires a Mac with Apple silicon (M1 or newer) and macOS 14 Sonoma or later. The installer says Kapitsa runs on Macs with Apple silicon only.

name: Trivy
description: Open-source Apache-2.0 scanner for vulnerabilities, misconfigurations, and secrets across container images, Kubernetes, and code repositories.
use_cases: Finding misconfigurations and secrets in repos
pricing: Free, open source (Apache 2.0).
verdict_reason: Trivy is for developers who want one open-source scanner for vulnerabilities, misconfigurations, and secrets. The project README lists container images, filesystems, remote git repositories, virtual machine images, and Kubernetes as targets. The license is Apache-2.0.
mobile_note: The official site doesn't mention a mobile app or mobile use, so this isn't confirmed.
mobile_description: The official site doesn't mention a mobile app or mobile use.

name: Infisical
description: Open-source secrets manager with a self-hostable MIT core. Agent Vault lets AI agents such as Claude Code, Codex, and OpenCode call APIs without holding the keys.
use_cases: Letting agents call APIs without holding keys
pricing: Secrets Management free tier $0 (5 identities); Pro $20/month per identity billed annually ($23 monthly); Advanced $40/month per identity billed annually ($46 monthly); Enterprise custom. MIT core is free to self-host. Agent Vault includes 5,000 requests a month, then $2 per 1,000.
verdict_reason: Infisical is for teams that want application secrets, and for agents that need to call APIs without holding the keys. The site says the core is open source under the MIT license and can be self-hosted. Agent Vault attaches the credential at the network boundary so the agent never holds it, and the homepage lists Claude Code, Codex, and OpenCode among the agents that work with it. Secrets Management has a free tier at $0 for 5 identities. Paid plan prices are on the pricing page.
mobile_note: The official site doesn't mention a mobile app or mobile use, so this isn't confirmed.
mobile_description: The official site doesn't mention a mobile app or mobile use.
